beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps super-resolution output dense while a compact DQ-CTM thought process updates the representation through shared recurrent ticks.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The method separates the dense image representation from the compact computation that updates it. The encoder converts the low-resolution image into a dense feature carrier. Windowing groups the carrier for local processing while preserving its tokens. The DQ-CTM thought process updates each window through repeated ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense field into the final high-resolution output.

beats.intent: The carrier equation first makes a dense feature field from the low-resolution image, then partitions that field into windows without changing the token set.
beats.narration: The dense carrier is explicit, so the compact thought process does not replace the spatial field. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into that carrier. The window partition operates on the carrier and keeps the tokens available for update.

params.headline: The carrier stays dense before the thought process runs

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; at 1.129 million parameters, it is second largest among the five methods.
beats.claim: DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129M parameters in Table 1, behind CARN and above IMDN, RFDN, and CATANet.
beats.narration: The parameter counts show that this result is not mainly a claim about being cheap. CATANet is the smallest of the five methods. RFDN and IMDN are also smaller than DQ-CTM-SR. DQ-CTM-SR is the second largest at 1.129 million parameters. CARN is the largest at 1.592 million parameters.
